hero.title: WizardScape
hero.p: A 3D mobile survival prototype featuring auto-cast combat and dynamic power-up systems.

img.alt: The banner of the prototype 'WizardScape: The Magic Chase'

points.1: WizardScape is a technical prototype developed to explore the 'Reverse Bullet Hell' genre on mobile devices using Unreal Engine 5.4.
points.2: The project focuses on the core pillars of the genre: autonomous combat logic, high-density enemy spawning, and a data-driven meta-progression shop.
points.3: As a Pre-Alpha demo, it served as a playground for optimizing C++ performance on Android while managing real-time stat modifiers.

points.1: Auto-Cast Combat: A circular proximity system that automatically targets and triggers spells against the closest threats.
points.2: Diamond Ecosystem: Multi-tiered resource collection: Blue (Currency), Green (Temporary Boosts), and Red (Challenge Modifiers).
points.3: Meta-Progression: A persistent shop system where players can spend collected resources to permanently upgrade wizard stats.
points.4: Dynamic Swarm: Procedural wave spawning with increasing enemy density and scaling difficulty over time.

points.1: Optimized Spawning: A C++ component-based spawner designed to handle high enemy counts efficiently.
points.2: Modifier Architecture: Flexible buff/debuff logic allowing gems to inject temporary or permanent stat changes.
points.3: Android Pipeline: Full integration with the modern Android SDK/NDK stack and customized Java setup for UE 5.4.
points.4: Collision Filtering: Specialized physics channels to manage interactions between the wizard, gems, and enemy mages.

points.1: Mobile-First HUD: Vertical UI layout optimized for one-handed play, featuring integrated experience bars and status icons.
points.2: Virtual Joystick: Custom-tuned touch input mapping to ensure fluid movement in high-pressure combat scenarios.
points.3: Asset Management: Systematic cleanup of unused resources and texture optimization to maintain stability on mobile hardware.

components.title: Modular Component Architecture
components.desc: The player character's logic is decoupled into specialized C++ Actor Components. This modular approach ensures that systems like Health, Economy, and Spawning are independent, reusable, and easy to debug.
components.img1: Character Component Stack: A view of the BP_Character hierarchy showing the custom C++ components (Health, Money, Spawner) integrated into the main actor.
components.img2: Health & Loot Logic: Details of the HealthComponent. It manages vitals and handles the 'Spawn on Dead' logic, ensuring enemies drop specific gems with custom Z-axis offsets upon defeat.
components.img3: Dynamic Spawning System: The SpawnerComponent configuration. It manages enemy mage pools and randomized spawning patterns relative to the player's world position.

gems.title: Dynamic Resource Ecosystem
gems.desc: A probability-based spawning system for interactive resources. Using a polymorphic C++ hierarchy, gems deliver specific gameplay modifiers while maintaining a lightweight data footprint.
gems.img1: Spawner Configuration: A view of the BP_GemSpawner properties. It allows designers to assign weight-based probabilities (e.g., 55/45) to different actor classes, which the C++ backend then normalizes at runtime.
gems.img2: Polymorphic Hierarchy: Showcase of the three gem Blueprints. Each one inherits from a specialized C++ parent class (Buff, Debuff, Money), demonstrating a clean decoupling between core logic and data-only assets.
gems.img3: Technical Implementation: A snippet of the C++ spawning logic. It utilizes LineTraceSingleByChannel to detect the ground and SpawnActor to instantiate the chosen gem at the exact impact point.

shop.title: Modular Meta-Progression Shop
shop.desc: A scalable upgrade interface built using reusable custom widgets. The logic is driven by a C++ base class that automatically handles data propagation and event broadcasting via dynamic delegates.
shop.img1: Pre-Construct Data Binding: Analysis of the NativePreConstruct function. This logic ensures that descriptions, prices, and limits are automatically updated in the Viewport as soon as a designer changes the C++ properties.
shop.img2: Custom Item Component: The WBP_ShopItem widget, parented to the ShopItem C++ class. It encapsulates all individual button logic, including the FOnButtonPressedDelegate for centralized handling.
shop.img3: Shop Layout & Hierarchy: The main WBP_ShopPage hierarchy. It utilizes a Vertical Box to manage multiple instances of the custom item widget, demonstrating a clean and DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) UI architecture.
